thread:
katie-sales: Heads up — RegioBank (EU retail banking) requested a PoC evidence bundle. They want a clear EU-only processing attestation, a hosting boundary diagram, a BYOK/KMS flow, and the full subprocessor roster (with contract/SCC references). Need to hand something to their vendor-risk team by EOD Friday.

sam-arch: I can sketch a hosting boundary + minimal infra snippet. Clarify: they said no cross-border processing — do they permit multi-EU-region failover (eu-west-1 <-> eu-central-1) for resilience, or must we pin to a single region for the PoC? That changes the diagram.

katie-sales: Good question — RegioBank said in the call: "All processing must remain within EU territory for the PoC." Sounds like multi-EU-region failover is okay as long as it stays EU-only. For legal, treat it as EU-only and call out that multi-region within EU is optional. Also they asked for a Dedicated (reserved capacity) variant showing network isolation.

maria-security: Noted. Quick list of what we can supply today: Hosted (region-locked to EU) with TLS + KMS; Dedicated (customer VPC + private peering) with optional on-prem connector; BYOK/HSM options (customer-managed keys or HSM-wrapped keys) and exportable key-usage audit logs; subprocessor roster (we'll flag staff locations outside EU where applicable). We'll include a retention/logging matrix and mark which logs may contain hashed identifiers or PII.

jen-legal: From legal side I'll prepare: 1) Subprocessor roster CSV (name, role, primary-region, staff-locations, contract-ref (SCC/DPA link)), 2) A short EU-only PoC attestation letter describing contractual controls and region locks, 3) References to our SCC template and DPA. Note: BYOK requires a signed addendum about key custody terms.

sam-arch: Dropping a quick ASCII hosting sketch + a tiny infra config snippet for region enforcement — will convert to a PDF.

sam-arch:
```
[EU LB]
   |
[Redwood EU Cluster (eu-central-1, eu-west-1)]
   |-- Inference runtime pods (ephemeral, mem-only processing)
   |-- KV cache (region-local, no cross-region replication unless EU-failover enabled)
   |-- Object storage (bucketeu-*) - eu-only buckets

# region policy example (YAML):
region_policy:
  allowed_regions: [eu-central-1, eu-west-1]
  failover: eu-only
  enforce_strict: true
```

katie-sales: Perfect. Maria — can you add a short retention matrix and flag which logs might include token hashes/identifiers? RegioBank was specific about retention periods.

maria-security: Draft retention/logging matrix (will annotate PII exposure and pseudonymization):
- Request/ingress logs: 90 days (tokens redacted, request hashes stored)
- Key-usage/audit logs: 1 year (immutable, HSM-backed append-only store)
- Admin/operator audit trail: 2 years (full audit events)
- Metrics/telemetry: 30 days aggregated, 1 year summaries (no request-level identifiers)
I'll also include CAIQ references we usually attach.

ops-deploy-bot: Uploaded: eu-hosting-boundary-v1.pdf -> https://files.redwood.internal/eu-hosting-boundary-v1 (access: sales/legal)

jen-legal: Subprocessor CSV will include whether staff supports remotely from non-EU locations and whether SCCs are in place. If any subproc has staff outside EU who may access data, we will include mitigations (SLA terms, MFA, dedicated EU-only access controls) and mark them clearly.

sam-arch: Adding a BYOK/KMS pseudo-flow for the packet:
```
KMS_flow: {
  kms_mode: "BYOK",
  key_holder: "customer-kms-eu-central-1",
  wrap_mode: "HSM-wrap",
  audit_sink: "audit-logs-eu (immutable, retention=1y)"
}
```

maria-security: Quick note on logging: key-usage logs will show key IDs and operation types (encrypt/decrypt/sign) but not plaintext. We can export those logs to the customer's audit collector if they request.

jen-legal: I'll also draft a short attestation text we can sign that states: "For the scoped PoC, Redwood will process RegioBank data only within EU regions specified in the attached hosting boundary. No non-EU fallback will be used unless explicitly authorized in writing." Will attach SCC/DPA references and a BYOK addendum template.

katie-sales: Timeline: can we get an initial package (diagram PDF + subproc CSV + attestation draft + retention matrix) by EOD today? I'll send to legal@regiobank.com and cc sales@redwood.com.

sam-arch: I can produce the PDF and infra snippets in ~2 hours.

maria-security: I'll drop the annotated retention matrix + CAIQ mapping in ~90 minutes.

jen-legal: I'll prioritize the roster + attestation and aim to have draft by EOD today; final signed attestation can follow after internal approvals.

katie-sales: Thanks — please upload artifacts to the files bucket and post links here when ready. Also include a minimal 'how-to' for ops to enforce region_policy in the customer's PoC config.

ops-deploy-bot: Uploaded: subprocessor-roster-regiobank-v1.csv -> https://files.redwood.internal/subproc-roster-regiobank-v1 (access: sales/legal)

katie-sales: Got it. Once jen confirms the attestation I'll send the package. If RegioBank needs us to remove any subproc entirely for the PoC, we can propose the Dedicated option (isolated GPU pool + private peering + BYOK) as a higher-assurance deliverable.

maria-security: Adding that note to the pack. Also flagging any subprocessors that have remote support agents outside EU and offering mitigation language (contractual access controls, IP whitelisting, dedicated support window).

jen-legal: Draft attestation uploaded -> https://files.redwood.internal/regiobank-eu-poc-attestation-draft (access: sales/legal). Please review and comment.

katie-sales: Reviewing now. Great work team — this should cover the vendor-risk checklist for first pass. :thumbsup:

maria-security: I'll prepare the CAIQ mapping and attach it to the PDF package before you send.

sam-arch: Final note — include an ops config snippet to set region_policy at runtime and disable any non-EU model fallback paths. I'll add that to the hosting PDF.

katie-sales: Thanks all. I'll stand by for the final links and will schedule a short review with RegioBank if they want a quick walkthrough of the artifacts.
